# NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via direct thickness measurement or weight-loss tracking; my mechanism departs by inferring effective blade radius erosion from the existing wheel motor current and vibration sensor correlation, using media feed-rate as a normalized excitation proxy. The failure-physics connection is that blade mass loss shifts the wheel's moment of inertia and aerodynamic drag profile, altering motor current demand at fixed rpm while simultaneously changing the harmonic vibration signature due to shifting balance and media interaction forces.

# PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Wheel torque $T \propto I_{eff} \alpha + F_{drag}(R_{eff}, \dot{m})$. Blade erosion reduces $I_{eff}$ and $R_{eff}$, decreasing $F_{drag}$ for a given media flow rate $\dot{m}$, which lowers motor current $I_{motor}$. Concurrently, erosion-induced mass asymmetry increases unbalance force $F_{unb} \propto m_{def} r_{def} \omega^2$, raising vibration amplitude $V_{vib}$. Magnitude verification: For a 2800 rpm wheel, a 10% radius reduction causes ~5-8% torque drop (CALCULATED from $T \propto R^2$ for constant $\dot{m}$), detectable against motor baseline; corresponding vibration rise from unbalance is non-linear but monotonic. Both signals derive from ALREADY-RECORDED telemetry without new instrumentation.

# IMPLEMENTATION BILL
(a) Compute real-time normalized torque index $TI = I_{motor} / \dot{m}$ using ALREADY-RECORDED "wheel motor current" and "media feed-rate counter"; threshold set to 0.85x of initial commissioning baseline (DERIVED from stated machine specs and initial test data) indicating 15% effective radius loss.
(a) Extract dominant vibration harmonic at 1x wheel rpm from ALREADY-RECORDED "machine vibration sensor"; set threshold at 2.0x baseline RMS value (DERIVED from stated vibration sensor noise floor and initial balance check) indicating unbalance precursor.
(b) Configure logic gate: Erosion Warning = ($TI < 0.85 \times TI_{base}$) AND ($V_{vib} > 2.0 \times V_{base}$); both conditions must persist for 5 consecutive minutes (ASSUMPTION for transient filter) to prevent false trips.
(b) Output binary state to machine HMI: "BLADE EROSION PRECURSOR" when triggered, "NOMINAL" otherwise; no physical intervention, only indication.
(c) No new hardware; utilize existing "wheel motor current", "machine vibration sensor", and "media feed-rate counter" per user constraint "no new instrumentation, no camera on the wheel housing".

# BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
(a) Installability: SAME as standard practice (zero new sensors); only firmware code change on existing PLC/HMI, identical burden class to standard thickness-gauge retrofit but lower cost.
(a) Operability: SAME burden; automatic monitoring, no operator input required beyond reading HMI status, matching standard practice's automated indication burden.
(a) Maintenance: LOWER burden than standard thickness-gauge practice; no sensor calibration, no probe wear, no housing access for physical inspection, only software threshold maintenance.
(b) Rough Cost Class: SOFTWARE-ONLY vs. HARDWARE+SOFTWARE for standard practice; significantly cheaper, same feasibility class, different mechanism (inference vs. direct measurement).

# EXECUTABLE TEST
(a) Protocol: Run wheel at 100% rated media feed rate for 1 hour; record $I_{motor}$ and $V_{vib}$ baseline; then run at 50% media feed rate for 30 minutes; compute $TI$ ratio between two flow rates; verify $TI_{50\%} / TI_{100\%} \approx 1.0 \pm 5\%$ (ASSUMPTION for linear torque-flow relationship at fixed rpm) to validate current-feed normalization.
(a) Pass/Fail Thresholds: Test passes if normalized $TI$ stability is within 5% across flow rates and vibration harmonic isolation is >10 dB above noise floor; kill criterion: if $TI$ varies >10% with flow rate, mechanism invalid due to non-linear motor control interaction, abort implementation.
(a) Duration: 1.5 hours total; instruments: existing "wheel motor current", "media feed-rate counter", "machine vibration sensor"; validated against ALREADY-RECORDED data from initial commissioning logs.

# CONSTRAINT BIND
Primary stated indicator: "wheel motor current" normalized by "media feed-rate counter" is the PRIMARY indicator because torque drop from erosion is the direct physical consequence of mass loss; "machine vibration sensor" is SUPPLEMENTARY only, confirming unbalance onset before trip, never replacing the primary torque-based erosion inference. The predictor uses both per user constraint "use only the existing wheel motor current, machine vibration sensor and media feed-rate counter".
